parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity, and no documented visitor-facing entry screening, detention or capital exposure. Core exposures are documented: birth-sex housing of trans women in the capital's city jail, with mandatory head-shaving and gang 'weddings' as survival strategy; service and entry refusals of gender-diverse people with little consequence; and local ordinances restricting dress, with enforcement undocumented. There is no national SOGI anti-discrimination law, and the equality bill has stalled for 25 years. Protections are real but patchy: about nine provinces and 32 cities prohibit SOGI discrimination, harassment fines exist, and a city right-to-care card operates. Killings are raw counts with no denominator and carry no measured rate. Custody exposure applies only if the visitor is detained, and the annex practice is not shown to be general. Rated at Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented traveller-facing entry screening, marker-mismatch refusal or secondary inspection of foreign-document holders. Resident birth-sex marker rules do not govern visitors' home passports.
entry_documents.protection: No documented visitor-facing entry protection beyond the absence of a documented entry restriction.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry exposure would arise only if a document discrepancy led to investigation, which is not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Capital city jail houses trans women by birth sex in male dormitories, with mandatory head-shaving and gang-run 'weddings' used for protection. A press investigation (Dec 2022) documents this. A southern jail annex segregates LGBT detainees in batches, but this is not sourced as general practice.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Annex segregation at one southern jail is a partial, unsourced protective practice; no national placement rule is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Exposure is conditional on detention, but a detained visitor would likely face birth-sex placement with documented sexual-violence and hierarchy risk at the capital's city jail.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No national anti-discrimination statute; facility and service exclusion of gender-diverse people reported with little legal consequence. Local dress ordinances restrict expression in one southern city, enforcement undocumented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State/provincial SOGIE ordinances in about nine provinces and 32 cities; national human-rights commission investigates but cannot enforce.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local protections cover some localities and do not reach the national custody or dress-rule layer, so a visitor's protection depends on location.

care_services.exposure: No documented care denial to visitors. Gender-affirming care access for visitors is not documented, and the record contains no trans-specific health rule.
care_services.protection: A city right-to-care card lets registered LGBTQ couples make medical decisions through a power of attorney, rolled out to government hospitals. It does not cover trans identity directly.
care_services.interaction: Care protection is limited to registered couples and government hospitals, so a visiting single traveller is unlikely to benefit.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police arrested about 20 Pride participants in 2020 under communicable-disease and assembly statutes. A religious-community municipality bans cross-dressing under imprisonment, though enforcement is undocumented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Social-worker and women's/safe-spaces statutes penalise SOGIE harassment with fines and sometimes jail; the 2023 lawyers' code bars SOGI discrimination. Official apology after a 2024 drag attack shows some state condemnation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police-facing hostility is documented in protest settings; harassment protections exist but enforcement is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Family-imposed conversion therapy and hate crimes against LGBTQ teens of a religious group are documented, backed by an establishment. Minors can be held in birth-sex custody. Adopter 'good moral character' is open to interpretation.
minors_guardians.protection: School uniform policy matching gender identity and gender-responsive curriculum review since 2016–2017; a 2023 national social welfare and education policy.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's exposure rises with any family or guardian connection to the religious group and with custody exposure if detained; a guardian's adoption-fitness exposure is not directly relevant to a visit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans killings reported from at least 2012, including a June 2025 river death and a clinic shooting the same day. A foreigner was arrested for raping a trans woman in May 2025. Raw counts with no denominator give no rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Prosecution of a foreign attacker and public outcry after the 2024 and 2025 cases show some institutional response. Killings are not shown to be prosecuted as a class.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Killings are not treated as a rate; the national commission calls the pattern 'transfemicide' but without a denominator.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No national anti-discrimination statute; the equality bill died in the upper chamber and was rejected by government in 2022. No legal gender recognition, and surgery does not change legal gender. Discrimination remedies are patchy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Local SOGIE ordinances, harassment fines, the national human-rights commission, and a 2025 rights-based shift in some courts.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies do not reach the custody or national-level exposures, so remedies are limited for a visitor outside covered localities.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both use birth-sex housing in male blocks with assault risk and cross-dressing enforcement. This case scores higher because there is no documented criminal cross-dressing arrest of visitors and no capital provision. Protections are broader locally.

Both lack national anti-discrimination protection and document restrictive practice. This case scores slightly higher: no clear visitor-facing exclusion from schools or clinics, and custody exposure only applies when detained.

Both involve birth-sex placement with documented harm and partial denial. This case is similar in custody exposure but rates slightly higher because service and violence exposure is less frequent, and local protections and harassment fines operate.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is lenient at entry and in law, but the custody layer is hostile. Trans women in the capital's city jail face birth-sex male dormitories, forced head-shaving and gang-run protection arrangements, a risk a visitor faces only if detained. Service refusals and local dress ordinances add everyday exposure, and no national anti-discrimination statute backs the patchwork of localised SOGIE protections. The killings are reported without a denominator and are not rated as a rate. Protective machinery (local ordinances, harassment fines, school policy, prosecution of one attacker) operates unevenly and does not reach the custody layer, so the net rating sits in the Elevated band.
